hints.title: Left Root Right Ordering
hints.text: Process all nodes in the left subtree, followed by the current node value, and finally the right subtree.

hints.title: Simulating Call Frames
hints.text: Drill down along left children pushing nodes onto a collection, then pop to visit and turn to the right child.

hints.title: Iterative Traversal with Explicit Store
hints.text: Traverse tree with current pointer and a node container. While pointer is not null or container is non-empty, push current and advance left. When null is reached, pop the top node, append its value to the result list, and set current to its right child.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List, Optional

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

class Solution:
    def inorderTraversal(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> List[int]:
        res = []
        stack = []
        curr = root
        while curr or stack:
            while curr:
                stack.append(curr)
                curr = curr.left
            curr = stack.pop()
            res.append(curr.val)
            curr = curr.right
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Optimal linear traversal visiting every node once with call stack bounded by tree height.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursion with repeated array concatenation incurs quadratic O(N^2) time overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative stack traversal yields O(H) auxiliary space without recursion stack overflow.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Demonstrate iterative traversal with an explicit node stack alongside recursive understanding.
